title: Local algebra approximation systems with localized scalar extension transitions
statement: A local algebra approximation system consists of the following data, all in one common sufficiently large universe. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed preorder. Let $R_i,S_i,R,S$ be commutative local rings with local homomorphisms $\varphi_i:R_i\to S_i$, $\varphi:R\to S$, local transitions $r_{ji}:R_i\to R_j$, $s_{ji}:S_i\to S_j$ for $i\le j$, and local cocone maps $r_i:R_i\to R$, $s_i:S_i\to S$. Local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Transitions obey identities and composition, the cocones are compatible, and all squares involving the $\varphi_i$ and $\varphi$ commute. The specified cocones are ring colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; explicitly, every element comes from a stage and equality of two representatives is detected at a common later stage. Let $M_i$ be finite $S_i$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $M$ an $S$-module, with additive transitions $m_{ji}$ semilinear over $s_{ji}$ and additive cocone maps $\mu_i$ semilinear over $s_i$, obeying identities, composition and compatibility, with the specified cocone an abelian-group colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The $R_i$- and $R$-module structures are the restrictions through $\varphi_i$ and $\varphi$. Each $S_i$ is essentially of finite type over $R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. For each $i\le j$, the canonical homomorphism $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$, $a\otimes b\mapsto s_{ji}(a)\varphi_j(b)$, is a localization at some multiplicative subset: its elements become units, every target element is a fraction with a denominator in the subset, and a source element mapping to zero is killed by a member of the subset. The canonical scalar extension map $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to M_j$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a m_{ji}(x)$, is an isomorphism. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The coefficient action of $R_i$ on $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ is the canonical one with algebra map $R_i\xrightarrow{r_i}R\to k$.
